prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, and its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep my round-1 configuration: a single prize for B009 to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. After the full exchange, six of eight members name this same trio as their sole preferred configuration, and the remaining two prefer B026 while naming B009 as their alternative, so it is the only configuration no member rejects outright. I do not rest on that count. The scientific case is that Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal-invariant insulators with strong spin-orbit coupling fall into a Z2 class with protected edge states and no broken symmetry, and that Molenkamp's group then observed the predicted edge transport in HgTe quantum wells. Two decades of independent confirmation by transport, ARPES and STM, and spread into photonics, cold atoms and materials design, make the result mature. On the chair's question about the 2016 prize, the difference I would put in the citation is that 2016 honoured topological phase transitions and phases in model systems, while this prize honours a measurable invariant of real band structures, with a quantised edge signature in a specific material. On the third slot, I find Mele defensible because the Z2 invariant is the concept that underlies both the HgTe result and the later three-dimensional work, and the quantum spin Hall prediction is a joint Kane-Mele paper. I would not switch the third name to Hasan without also settling the 2D versus 3D question, which I would rather leave explicit than hide.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness and I do not think the citation can cure it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang identified HgTe, and Hasan's three-dimensional work is a separate and important step, so the trio leaves out serious claimants; the citation should therefore be limited to the quantum spin Hall state and its first realisation, and the committee's own text should state that the three-dimensional topological insulators and the HgTe proposal are not covered, rather than imply a complete history. The 2016 prize also gives a real basis for the incrementalism objection from Kroll and Danielsson, and my answer to it is a judgment, not a settled fact. Direct technological payoff is still limited. Against B026, the main point in its favour is the cleanest credit boundary on the shortlist, but I would still need the overlap with the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize argued, and the magic-wavelength priority is not verifiable from the materials we have.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B026 for Katori and Ye, with a clean two-name credit and concrete consequences, while saying that the overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes and unverified magic-wavelength priority are the main risks, and that B009's breadth of support is not simple momentum.
responses.response: I take the credit cleanliness of B026 seriously, and it is a better attribution than B009 can offer. But Kroll himself calls the overlap with the comb and ion-control prizes and the magic-wavelength priority the strongest objections, and the materials do not let us resolve either. I would accept B026 as an alternative, and I list it as such, because it is mature and a fair compromise if B009 does not carry. I will not put it first while its distinctness from 2005 and 2012 rests on recollection, whereas for B009 the committee can name the specific differences from 2016. I would also note that I do not regard the B009 gaps around BHZ and Hasan as trivial: they are a reason to word the citation narrowly, not a reason to prefer the other candidate.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that lattice clocks are distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes because the magic-wavelength idea and Ye's accuracy work are specific, and that the credited pair maps onto two identifiable contributions, while warning that B009 should not be treated as the committee's centre of gravity merely because of breadth.
responses.response: I agree that breadth of support is not merit and I have tried to argue B009 on its content. Her two-contribution mapping of Katori and Ye is persuasive, and I agree that the credit is cleaner than for B009. Where I part from her is on distinctness: an ion-clock partisan can say the best clocks are not uniquely lattice clocks, as she concedes, and a prize on precision timekeeping after 2005 and 2012 reads more as the next refinement than as a new discovery. I would give Lindroth a firm answer on one point from the chair's questions. If B026 does not carry I would regard it as a good alternative, not a poor one, so the committee is not forced into a choice between incompatible views.

responses.point: Johansson holds B009 as a clean prediction-then-observation story, says the credit is crowded because BHZ and Hasan are left out, and says that if no defensible 2D versus 3D split exists, B037 or B010 may give a cleaner configuration.
responses.response: I think the 2D versus 3D split is defensible if we say plainly what we credit. The quantum spin Hall state and its HgTe observation are one complete theory-plus-experiment step with a decisive experimental confirmation, whereas Hasan's three-dimensional work depends on that concept and is a further step, which a later year could consider. As for B037, her point that Zoller and Cirac recur across candidates, and that the proposed trios for B037 differ, is exactly why I think B037 is less ready than B009. I also accept her position that B010 should not be pressed this year; the 2025 prize makes it a timing question for me rather than an ineligibility, and I would not argue it is disqualified forever.

responses.point: Mehlig supports a single B009 prize to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as one theory part and one experimental part, but says that omitting BHZ and Hasan risks being judged unfair, and asks whether the citation can be fair to them.
responses.response: Mehlig's concern is the right one, and I would answer it by being explicit about scope in the citation and in the committee's own supporting text. The citation names the quantum spin Hall state, the Z2 classification and the HgTe observation, and does not claim the three-dimensional materials. I do not think this fully removes the unfairness to BHZ and Hasan, and I would not pretend it does. It is the narrowest wording that does not credit the trio with work it did not do. I would also not support enlarging the configuration to a second part for the sake of fairness, since the three-person limit makes a fair split impossible and every member favours a single part.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B009 first but raises the third slot (Mele or Hasan) and whether B009 is sufficiently distinct from the 2016 prize, and notes that his attributions rest on recollection.
responses.response: I agree with Danielsson that the third slot and the 2016 relationship are the two points on which the committee should be clear, and I have tried to answer both above. On the 2016 prize I would add that the incrementalism objection loses force because the committee can state the difference in one sentence in the citation: the first prize concerns topological order in model systems, this one a topological invariant in real materials with an observable edge channel. On IceCube, I accept his earlier point that a single name for a large collaboration and partial source identification make B024 premature for this year, and I now treat it as a case for later and not as my alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee, on the 2D versus 3D question, will accept a narrow quantum spin Hall and HgTe citation without Hasan or the BHZ proposers
Whether the 2016 prize makes B009 read as a follow-on despite the distinction between model systems and a topological invariant of real materials
Whether Mele or Hasan is the right third name, which depends on the 2D versus 3D judgment
Whether B026 lattice clocks can be separated from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and whether the magic-wavelength priority holds, neither of which I can verify from the supplied materials
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B009 or B026. My documented collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur) are in astroparticle physics and instrumentation. B024 (IceCube) is in my general research area, but no documented tie to IceCube or Francis Halzen is recorded, and it is no longer part of my preferred configuration or alternatives. I have no recorded tie to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Katori, Ye or the other credited names.
